label: sprites/fw_steam.spr: a steam puff that rises and thins, animated

againstClass.words: flickers: more coherence from frame to frame

R1.reason: It reads as a steam or smoke puff. It starts as a small bright white puff in frame 1, swells into a grey-white cloud by frames 5-6, then breaks up and thins away in frames 8-10, which is the effect the brief asks for. There are slightly hard dark crack lines inside the puff in frames 3-7 (a crease running down its middle) that make it look a bit carved, but not enough to make it read as a different effect.

R2.reason: At 64x96 the frames suit a tall rising puff. The mean border measure (0.004) is inside the smoke-puff range. But the border maximum of 0.316 shows that at least one frame runs into its edge, and the sheet bears this out: in frames 7-8 the expanded cloud reaches the sides of its cell and the edge looks cut off rather than fading out. The puff also spreads mostly sideways and in place rather than climbing up the tall frame, so the upper part of the 96-high frame stays empty in the early frames and the effect does not fill the frame the way a rising puff should.

R3.reason: Neutral white to grey throughout, bright when dense and dimming as it thins. Blended additively this gives a pale steam colour with no tint, which fits the brief's industrial palette and Half-Life's own steam and smoke sprites. No colour measurement fails.

R4.reason: The envelope measures pass: 12 frames, peak at 0.45, and both the first and last frames are dark, so the one-shot ends dark. But jitter is 1.52, outside the smoke-puff class's range of 0.9-1.5 ('flickers: more coherence from frame to frame'), so this item cannot score 2. The pictures show the same problem: between frames 7, 8 and 9 the cloud does not thin smoothly but falls apart into scattered patches, and it jumps from a dense cloud in 8 to a few faint specks in 9. The upward motion the brief asks for is also weak: the puff grows more than it rises.

R5.reason: Saved as sprites/fw_steam.spr, the name the brief asks for. It is parallel and additive, the usual type and format for Half-Life's steam and smoke puffs, with 12 frames at 64x96 as measured. Nothing indicates it fails to read back.
